doc_verification.detail: Reachability: PASS — constraint source_url https://qdrant.tech/documentation/manage-data/payload/ retrieved with full page content (WebFetch was domain_blocked by the sandbox network policy; the session's web reader tool fetched the page successfully, so the URL is live, not dead). Version: PARTIAL — concept page carries no version routing (doc_version 'current (site latest; no version archive)'); endpoint face aligned via versioned v-1-18-x api-reference in the registry. Content: PARTIAL — the geo literal-format promise IS documented on this exact page ('Coordinate should be described as an object containing two fields: `lon` - for longitude, and `lat` - for latitude', all examples numeric), but (a) 'of doubles' is example-inferred, never stated in prose, (b) the page never promises 4xx rejection of non-conforming literals at set-payload time, and (c) the SAME page explicitly declares 'Qdrant allows you to store any information that can be represented using JSON' and 'If the stored value type does not fit the filtering condition - it will be considered not satisfied' (filter-side disposition, documented). Endpoint: PASS — payload+set is in the endpoint_registry (api.qdrant.tech v-1-18-x points/set-payload, verified 2026-09-02, 'Points OR filter must identify the targets (both null is an error); returns 200 ok, 400, 404') and the constraint's own source_url page documents the Set payload REST schema for this exact route. REST+SDK examples co-exist on the page but the constraint is endpoint-level and the attack used REST — no confusion.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: payload/filter literal formats: geo point = {lon, lat}; datetime = RFC 3339 string; uuid = uuid string; arrays are same-typed
contract_grounding.note: E5 self-check: the observed value {"lon": "4.9", "lat": 52.37} is INSIDE the quote's constraint domain (a geo payload literal on payload+set) and non-compliant (lon is a string; the constraint description and the doc's all-numeric examples give lon/lat as numbers) — the value is not compliant, so violates=true is the honest reading. The competing doc-level free-JSON declaration ('store any information that can be represented using JSON') is recorded in doc_verification.content_consistency for the auditor to weigh as a by-design defense; it does not change the ingestion-face violation boolean. source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST POST /collections/{name}/points/payload -> SetPayloadShadow -> TryFrom<SetPayloadShadow> for SetPayload (validates ONLY points-or-filter presence; none of the payload VALUE formats) -> lib/shard/src/update.rs:716 set_payload -> Segment::set_payload merge of Payload(Map<String,Value>) (lib/segment/src/types.rs:2012, arbitrary JSON, persisted byte-equal) — no geo/datetime/uuid literal validation exists anywhere on the ingestion path. Lazy typed channels convert via Option: GeoMapIndex::get_value (geo_index/mod.rs:428, as_f64()->None => value silently skipped from the index, index create 200) and ValueChecker for GeoRadius/GeoBoundingBox/GeoPolygon (condition_checker.rs:245-296, as_f64()->None => check returns false 'not satisfied'); datetime indexer identical (numeric_index/mod.rs:1055, from_str().ok()).
source_grounding.outcome_note: The contract-required validation (reject a payload geo literal whose lon/lat are not numeric doubles) is absent from the entire ingestion path — the API accepts and byte-persists {"lon":"4.9"} with 200. Per the v3.4 tightened rule this is NOT marked by_design_in_source: no code comment, docstring, or in-source maintainer declaration of intent exists on the ingestion path (greps for intentionally/by-design/we-don't-validate/arbitrary-JSON comments across payload_ops.rs, payload_storage/, geo_index/ returned zero hits). The by-design DEFENSE that does exist is documentation-level ('store any information that can be represented using JSON' + filter-side 'considered not satisfied') — recorded in doc_verification.content_consistency for the auditor to weigh; it lives in the doc layer, not the source.
